title: Incident Handler
description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth - personal, professional, and financial - is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission - operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today - and we’re just getting started.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey’s products sit at the intersection of frontier AI, sensitive customer data, and critical business workflows. Our customers trust us to protect their information in an always-accelerating threat ecosystem, and security is how we foremost earn and keep our customers’ trust. We’re hiring an experienced Incident Response Handler to drive and ultimately lead incident response for security events. You will command incidents, coordinate containment, and enforce that real fixes are implemented, preventing recurrence. You’ll join a small, highly technical security team early in standing up a dedicated Detection & Response function, with real latitude to define how Harvey does incident response for years to come. Like the rest of Harvey’s security team, our program is built on offensive security experience - most engineers come from red-team, pentesting, or incident-response backgrounds, and we bring an attacker’s mindset to detection and response. This is an individual contributor role for someone who has operated in mature security organizations at leading technology companies and wants to help define incident response at one of the most important AI companies in the world.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Build strong relationships with key employees across the organization

- Participate in security incidents, leading investigations across cloud infrastructure, identity systems, corporate environments, and our AI platforms.

- Use, maintain, and contribute to an internally developed agentic SOC, fine tuned to Harvey’s threat environment

- Work cross functionally across technical and operational orgs, ensuring the right PRs ship and best policies are enforced

- Contribute to Harvey’s Detection & Response roadmap, including metrics, SLAs, threat modeling, and tabletop exercises for our most critical business risks.

- Work across teams to ensure incident follow ups are meaningfully closed

- Mentor engineers and incident responders, build playbooks and operational standards, and raise the security bar across the company.

WHAT YOU HAVE

- 3+ years of experience in Incident Response, Detection & Response, Security Operations, Threat Detection, or related security engineering disciplines.

- Experience participating in investigations and response efforts for complex security incidents in cloud-native environments.

- Deep understanding of attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures (MITRE ATT&CK and modern threat actor tradecraft).

- Experience with one or more major cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), plus strong knowledge of operating systems, networking, and identity systems.

- Experience building security automation and tooling, with strong scripting or software engineering skills in Python, Go, or similar languages.

Our high-performance culture is what allows us to drive sustained growth. Stronger together, we promote an environment where individuals can thrive.
Senior Analyst, Credit & Risk
About the Role
World Fuel is seeking a Senior Analyst, Credit & Risk to support credit underwriting, risk management, and working‑capital protection across our North American Land wholesale portfolios. This role plays a key part in evaluating the creditworthiness of new and existing counterparties, analyzing financial risk exposure, and enabling informed commercial decision‑making.
In addition to core underwriting responsibilities, this role supports process and system alignment between PDI and Oracle ERP platforms and provides oversight of an outsourced credit team. The position operates with a high degree of independence while partnering closely with Commercial, Legal, and Finance stakeholders and reports to the Director of NA Land Credit & Risk.
What You’ll Do

• Review and manage inbound credit requests through Kissflow queues to ensure timely and accurate decisions

• Analyze customer financial statements and supporting documentation to recommend credit limits and assess default risk

• Evaluate mark‑to‑market (MTM) exposure and forward trading activity with customers and suppliers

• Determine appropriate credit support and security requirements to mitigate risk

• Partner closely with Commercial and Legal teams to address credit‑related matters for new and existing customers

• Support the establishment and ongoing enforcement of credit policies, underwriting standards, and loss‑control procedures

• Gather, review, and analyze customer information to support credit recommendations

• Assist in standardizing credit reporting, customer credit profiles, and data analysis across platforms

• Contribute to initiatives that improve transparency, reduce handoffs, and enhance the timeliness of bad‑debt reserves and write‑offs

• Support system and process alignment between PDI and Oracle ERP environments following system migrations

• Oversee the daily activities of an outsourced credit team to ensure consistency and accuracy

• Perform ad hoc analysis and special projects as needed

What You Bring

• Strong experience analyzing financial statements and underwriting credit risk

• Working knowledge of forward trading concepts and mark‑to‑market exposure

• Advanced Excel skills with strong attention to detail

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook); Power BI is a plus

• Experience with PDI and/or Oracle ERP systems preferred

• Strong analytical, organizational, and time‑management skills

• Ability to collaborate effectively across cross‑functional teams

• Customer‑focused mindset with balanced risk judgment

• Sound business judgment and the ability to make data‑driven credit decisions

• Continuous‑improvement mindset with a willingness to challenge the status quo

Education & Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field required

• 3+ years of experience in credit, risk, or accounting, preferably within commodities, energy, or trading environments

We raised a $250M Series C to build the search engine for AIs. Led by a16z, with existing investors Benchmark, Lightspeed, and YC doubling down, the round brings Exa's valuation to $2.2 billion.

Exa is building a search engine for the AI era. Our Search API currently powers Agents, Fortune 500s, and AI labs as we transform an industry that hasn't been disrupted since the 90s. We're a largely SF-based team of ~100 from Harvard, MIT, Meta, Google Research, ex-founders, and dropouts alike. We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We're high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Support Engineers make sure every committed Exa customer gets their problem solved, fast, around the clock. We run support AI-first: AI tools like Pylon and agents triage tickets, answer them and resolve what they can. You take on what the AI can't: the hard, ambiguous technical problems that need a real engineer.

You'll have the same technical depth as our Forward Deployed Engineers. You'll dig into the API, SDKs and customers' integrations, reproduce bugs, and open pull requests with fixes for our engineers to review. When a problem truly needs Engineering, you escalate it with everything they need to act, and you stay the customer's point of contact until it's resolved. This is not a script-reading role. You are an engineer who owns the fix.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Build the support system: configure our Pylon instance and set up robust ticket tracking, SLA tracking and automations that make the support function as efficient as possible

- Resolve the tickets the AI can't, troubleshooting across the API, SDKs and customer integrations

- Spot patterns across tickets and turn them into product feedback and fixes

- Several years of hands-on programming experience. You can read and debug unfamiliar code, and you're comfortable opening pull requests in a production codebase

- Experience troubleshooting APIs, SDKs or distributed systems in production, ideally with search, retrieval, LLMs or data pipelines

- A structured approach to ambiguous problems: you ask the right questions, form hypotheses and test them

- Clear judgment on when to keep digging and when to escalate, and the ability to explain a technical problem clearly to customers and engineers

- Comfort working AI-first, with AI tools and agents as part of your daily workflow

- Availability for shift work as part of a 24/7, follow-the-sun support model

- Have built with LLMs, RAG or agents, and can reason about retrieval and search quality

- Have built automations or AI workflows that took repetitive work off a team

title: Senior Software Architect, AI Networking
description:
An applied research team within NVIDIA ’s Networking Systems & Software Architecture group is solving some of AI’s hardest infrastructure problems. The team builds systems-level software that moves data between GPUs, nodes, and storage at the speed modern AI demands-spanning low-level transport optimization, hardware-software co-design, and communication frameworks that plug directly into production AI stacks. The team's charter expands into emerging domains including quantum computing interconnects.
The Senior Architect role is to own modules and projects end-to-end-from scoping research questions to shipping production code. It calls for a recognized expert who drives technical decisions, pulls in ideas from research and industry, and regularly prototypes new approaches to prove a point. The work lives at the boundary of applied research and production engineering!

• Architecting and implementing high-performance communication and memory management libraries for distributed AI

• Driving hardware-software co-optimization with GPU, DPU, NIC, and switch teams through GPUDirect RDMA, NVLink, and next-generation interconnects

• Profiling and optimizing data movement across GPU memory, system DRAM, NVMe, and network fabrics

• Integrating networking capabilities into AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM

• Contributing to and maintaining open-source projects, mentoring engineers, conducting design reviews, and prototyping experimental technologies to evaluate their viability

What we need to see:

• 12+ years in systems software and/or networking with demonstrated ownership of complex projects.

• MS, PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

• Solid understanding of high-performance networking: InfiniBand, RoCE, RDMA, NVLink, GPUDirect.

• Strong C/C++/Rust systems programming with comfort in performance profiling and low-level debugging.

• Understanding of ML systems concepts-transformer architectures, KV cache mechanics, model parallelism, or distributed training and inference patterns.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Knowledge of ML inference frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) and their communication requirements.

• Knowledge of storage networking (NVMe-oF, GPUDirect Storage, S3).

• Background of Reinforcement Learning systems.

Directly reporting to a Site Leader, OAs play an essential role at Gopuff that requires drive, perseverance, positivity, and enthusiasm for the challenge. You will accomplish a variety of warehouse responsibilities including picking, packing, receiving product, and working with our delivery riders.
Customers turn to Gopuff to provide their everyday essentials-day and night, rain or shine. We're assembling a team of thinkers, dreamers and risk takers who are ready to help us reshape the world of retail faster than ever before. And it doesn't hurt if you like snacks.

#LI-DNP

At Gopuff, we know that life can be unpredictable. Sometimes you forget the milk at the store, run out of pet food for Fido, or just really need ice cream at 11 pm. We get it-stuff happens. But that’s where we come in, delivering all your wants and needs in just minutes.

And now, we’re assembling a team of motivated people to help us drive forward that vision to bring a new age of convenience and predictability to an unpredictable world.

Like what you’re hearing? Then join us on Team Blue.

Gopuff is an equal employment opportunity employer, committed to an inclusive workplace where we do not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, gender, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital or familial status, age, ancestry, disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. We believe in diversity and encourage any qualified individual to apply.

• Review Continuous Vetting alerts submitted through authorized channels.

• Utilize government-furnished systems to verify whether alerts are new, valid, and properly attributed to the correct subject.

• Identify, document, and assess issues that triggered each alert in accordance with federal vetting guidelines and contract-defined workflows.

• Recommend and record appropriate follow up actions necessary to support issue resolution, ensuring compliance with federal investigative standards.

• Input and update case, subject, and investigative details in multiple government systems and databases.

• Cross train across functional areas and provide surge or support coverage to meet contract service levels and mission needs.

• High school diploma or equivalent.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to interpret procedure manuals, email correspondence, and detailed instructions.

• Capability to manage and complete assignments independently with minimal supervision.

• Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.

• Must be able to work a flexible schedule based on workload demands, including potential evening and weekend hours.

• Must consent to a government background investigation.

• U.S. citizenship required due to contract requirements.

• Ability to work a 40+ hour schedule.

• Must reside within the Eastern Time Zone.

Work will be performed primarily in a remote capacity. If the employee resides within a one hour driving distance of Iron Mountain in Boyers, PA, occasional on site attendance may be required. NOTE: Orientation will be performed on-site at Iron Mountain, Boyers, PA, ASRC Federal PMO office.

• Work is performed using company furnished laptop or desktop. Position requires the ability to sit for extended periods of time.

• Ability to walk extended distance to work department when working on-site or use of bus transportation.

• Other physical activity may include reaching, bending, lifting, finger dexterity and repetitive motion.

NetImpact Strategies is seeking a Senior Functional Specialist to join our delivery team supporting Federal clients. The ideal candidate combines client-facing leadership skills with hands-on functional expertise, bridging the gap between business needs and technical implementation. This role will lead delivery activities, manage project scope and timelines, and work directly with stakeholders to define and document business requirements, ensuring successful outcomes aligned with mission objectives. Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle - creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

You own a portfolio of Kyra's largest enterprise accounts (multi-million-dollar brand partnerships) and you're measured on whether they grow. Retention, expansion, and Net Revenue Retention are your scoreboard.

- AI-native. You build AI tools into your daily work for faster execution, sharper insight, and smarter workflows

- You should be commercially sharp, operationally reliable, and able to speak confidently about the revenue impact of the accounts you've managed.

Traits That Matter

Curious. Commercially aware. Direct. Adaptable. Strong at building trust. Open to feedback. You don't avoid hard conversations. You don't wait for issues to escalate. You don't need constant direction.

HERE combines global location data, enterprise-grade technology and deep real-world context. You will help customers use those capabilities to optimize movement, improve operations, build location-aware products and apply AI to problems in the physical world. The expected base salary range for this position is $154,000 - $220,000 per year. Actual compensation will be based on factors such as skills and experience. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, which is subject to company and individual performance.

title: Director, Organic Growth & Discovery
description:
Who is Credible ?

Credible is a leading U.S. consumer finance marketplace, transforming the way consumers access and compare financial products. We operate at a consumer and enterprise level. On the consumer side, we help millions of people make smarter financial decisions by comparing personalized, pre-qualified offers across student loans, personal loans, mortgages, credit cards, and insurance - all without impacting their credit score. On the enterprise side, we power financial product comparison and distribution through deep integrations and partnerships with lenders, insurance carriers, and financial institutions, as well as providing marketplace technology and capabilities to third-party partners and distribution channels.

About the Role:
Credible is seeking an analytical, product-minded leader to own how consumers discover Credible online. The way people find financial products is evolving at a rapid pace. Search is turning into AI answers, and the decision to compare a loan or an insurance policy is moving beyond Google to AI platforms, Reddit, YouTube, or TikTok. We are uniquely positioned to be the trusted answer wherever that search begins.
In this role, you will own and scale organic discovery across Credible .com and our tier-1 publishing partners. SEO is the foundation but; the role spans everything SEO is becoming: traditional search, AI answer engines, and social and community platforms. You will also own the performance of the pages that organic traffic lands on, turning visits into completed applications through rigorous conversion rate optimization.
This is a highly visible role, both inside Credible and across our publisher partner network. You’ll work cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Editorial, Partnerships, and Paid Marketing, while leading a team of SEO and content specialists. The ideal candidate is deeply analytical, thinks like a product manager, and is grounded in revenue-based decisions. They can explain in dollars what happened, why it happened, and what we’re doing about it. You will thrive in a fast-moving environment and are passionate about helping consumers make great financial decisions.
Key Responsibilities:

• Own and lead Credible ’s organic discovery strategy across Credible .com and our tier-1 publishing partners, spanning SEO, AI platforms (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews), and social and community platforms (Reddit, YouTube, TikTok).

• Win visibility in AI-generated answers by understanding how large language models retrieve, summarize, and cite content, making our pages and product data easy to use and cite, and building presence in the off-site sources those models draw on, including forums, publishers, and earned media.

• Lead technical SEO at scale, including crawlability, indexation, site architecture, Core Web Vitals, structured data, and schema, partnering closely with our Content Platform engineering team.

• Own conversion rate optimization for organic entry pages: set page and template requirements, build and run a disciplined A/B testing program, and partner with Product to improve the journey from first visit to completed application.

• Act as a product owner for organic experiences, writing clear requirements, prioritizing a roadmap with Product and Engineering, and shipping improvements that move both traffic and conversion.

• Bring analytical rigor to every decision: separate competitive non-brand traffic from brand and direct demand, tie organic performance to revenue, and diagnose changes in performance down to the query, page, and funnel stage.

• Establish clear measurement frameworks that track leading indicators and long-term outcomes, including rankings, AI citations and share of voice, conversion rate, and revenue per visit.

• Reporting to leadership and stakeholders, with clear communication on KPIs, initiatives, and overall portfolio performance.

• Build authority through digital PR, expert contributors, and partner content

title: Controls Engineer, Power Generation
description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design and integrate automation systems for on-site power generation serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement.

Travel: 50%

Responsibilities

- Define control-system architecture, functional design specifications, sequences of operation, cause-and-effect matrices, alarm philosophy, and interface requirements.

- Integrate OEM controls, PLCs, DCS, SCADA, historian, microgrid controllers, protection systems, and data center BMS or EPMS platforms.

- Develop and review I/O lists, network architecture, control narratives, graphics, alarm limits, interlocks, permissives, and fail-safe behavior.

- Coordinate synchronization, load sharing, islanding, black start, load shedding, restoration, and generation-to-data-center operating modes.

- Evaluate cybersecurity, redundancy, time synchronization, communications protocols, data quality, and remote-support requirements.

- Lead or support software reviews, simulator testing, factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, commissioning, and tuning.

- Troubleshoot control-system and plant-performance issues and convert findings into corrective actions and reusable standards.

- Partner with electrical, mechanical, CSA, IT, security, operations, OEM, EPC, and data center controls teams.

Qualifications

- 8+ years of controls, automation, or instrumentation engineering experience in power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure.

- Strong experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration.

- Knowledge of generation controls, synchronization, load sharing, protective interfaces, process control, and safety interlocks.

- Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

- Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

- Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices.

- Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Skills

- Experience with major turbine or reciprocating-engine control platforms and microgrid controllers.

- Experience with IEC 61850, Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols.

- Experience integrating generation controls with BMS, EPMS, DCIM, or utility systems.

- Professional Engineer license, functional-safety training, or industrial-cybersecurity certification.
